knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=5x-1.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (5) \\  & =-\frac{5}{2\sqrt{(5x-1{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{1-4x}$ at the point where $x=-2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=1-4x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-4) \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-2} & ={(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4x}})|}_{x=-2} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4(-2)}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=3{x}^{2}+12x.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x+12.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (6x+12) \\  & =-\frac{6x+12}{2\sqrt{(3{x}^{2}+12x{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-6.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot -6 \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{-6x+7}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6{x}^{2}-12x}}$ at the point where $x=-4$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=6{x}^{2}-12x.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=12x-12.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (12x-12) \\  & =-\frac{12x-12}{2\sqrt{(6{x}^{2}-12x{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-4} & ={(-\frac{12x-12}{2\sqrt{(6{x}^{2}-12x{)}^{3}}})|}_{x=-4} \\  & =-\frac{12(-4)-12}{2\sqrt{(6(-4{)}^{2}-12(-4){)}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{60}{2\sqrt{{144}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{5}{288}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+21x}}$ at the point where $x=4$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u={x}^{2}+21x.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x+21.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (2x+21) \\  & =-\frac{2x+21}{2\sqrt{({x}^{2}+21x{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & ={(-\frac{2x+21}{2\sqrt{({x}^{2}+21x{)}^{3}}})|}_{x=4} \\  & =-\frac{2(4)+21}{2\sqrt{((4{)}^{2}+21(4){)}^{3}}} \\  & =-\frac{29}{2\sqrt{{100}^{3}}} \\  & =-\frac{29}{2000}.\end{aligned}
$$
